title: IT Service Management: Incidents, Problems, Changes and SLAs
oneLiner: Incidents, service requests, problems and changes in plain English, severity levels, SLAs, SLOs and error budgets, running a major incident, blameless postmortems, the 5 whys and change management.
keyTakeaway: Restore service first (incident), then remove the cause (problem). Agree what each severity means before you need it, give a major incident a commander and regular updates, and follow it with a blameless postmortem whose actions have owners and dates. Most outages follow a change, so changes need a plan and a way back.
explanation:
IT and operations teams run on tickets, and the vocabulary comes from ITIL. This lesson explains the processes you'll work in, without the certification jargon: the kinds of ticket, how severity and SLAs set priorities, how a major incident runs, and how teams learn from one afterwards.

It finishes with change management and how to write a ticket someone can act on straight away.
